title: sail count and sail names rescan the input when a current index is beside it
body:
`sail count` and `sail names` on the indexed backend never read the `.saidx` beside the input. `count.rs` calls `Index::build` and `names.rs` calls `Index::build_named`, so each run scans the whole input even when a current index file sits beside it. The commands that read through `indexed!` go through `index_of` in `input.rs`, which reads a current index.

`index::count_in` reads the count from the index header alone. A named index file carries the names, so `names` could read them without touching the data file.

Found while writing the test for sail-33353c. Those two commands do not refuse a stale index, because they never look at one.
